findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any hand soap available at the handsink along the main cookline. Shown to the PIC and soap was added to the dispenser to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always soap available at every handsink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Various salad dressings, potato salad, cut melon, and desserts were stored inside of a cooler with an ambient temperature of 50F. The foods were probed using several different internal thermometers. All TCS foods were discarded to correct the violation. The items had been stored in the unit since the morning, as far as the manager was aware. Ensure that TCS foods that are intended to be cold held are held at 41F or less. 

Also, ensure that shredded cheese that is being held on ice is changed frequently to avoid cheese from sitting in the temperature danger zone for long periods of time.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The cooler along the cookline that stores salad dressings had an ambient temperature of 50F. The inspector’s probe thermometer, the facility’s internal thermometer (recently placed inside of the unit), and the facility’s probe thermometer all verified an ambient temperature of 50F. The cooler stores salad dressing, uncooked broccoli, potato salad, fruit, and desserts. All time/temperature control(TCS) foods were pulled from the cooler and discarded. Per phone call with the facility’s manager, Don Hubbell, a service technician will be to service the cooler tomorrow morning. Ensure that cold holding equipment is sufficient enough to maintain cold hold temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for cross contamination and glove use. Incorrect sanitizer product was available for use at the 3 part sink dispenser, and staff initially thought the test strips were not working properly (see #28 & #48 for details). An active fruit fly population is present, and the current conditions in the dish area and at the drive thru are contributing to the issue. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at followup inspections.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) PIC switched tasks from working with an electronic device for inventory at the sandwich prep cooler to preparing orders without a glove change. Gloves were changed at request of inspector. Ensure gloves are immediately changed when switching tasks and prior to handling food after touching general surfaces with gloved hands. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Fruit flies were observed on clean dishes and shelving to the left of the dish machine. All dishes were to go through ware washing process again, and shelving needs to be cleaned and sanitized. Fruit flies were also observed on surfaces throughout the drive thru cabinet including around packaged single service articles. Management was encouraged to relocate single service articles until flies are no longer present in the drive thru cabinet. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Quat sanitizer is currently connected to the dispenser at the 3 part sink, and facility has labeling, test strips, and infographics posted at the 3 part sink for Sink and Surface Cleaner Sanitizer, which has different active ingredients of DDBSA/lactic acid. PIC did not realize the wrong product was connected to the dispenser and plans to confirm ordering of correct sanitizer with order that will be placed tomorrow for Saturday delivery. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 1) Facility has an active fruit fly population. The majority of flies were observed in the dish area and within the cabinet under the counter along the north wall at the drive thru. Dozens of fruit flies were observed under the sprayer sink on the plumbing and around the floor drain where heavy accumulation of mold and other debris was observed. Fruit flies were also observed on the walls around the dish machine, the clean dish shelving and dishes to the left of the dish machine, and surfaces to the left of the clean dish shelving. Dozens of fruit flies were also present under the soda machine ice bin in the drive thru cabinet and throughout the entirety the cabinet on shelving/brackets and surfaces of equipment said to be unused.
2) The current conditions in the dish area and the cabinet at the drive thru, specifically the absence of proper drainage from the ice bin, are contributing factors to the issue with fruit flies. The need for cleaning and general maintenance to aid in fly management were discussed. PIC was also advised on use of an enzymatic drain cleaner to remove buildup in floor drains that could be contributing to the fly issue.
In addition to cleaning and maintenance, management needs to get in touch with pest control operator for service. 
The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the premises by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the premies for evidence of pests; (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat sanitizer was in use and test strips were not available for verifying concentration. DDBSA/lactic acid strips were available for use, as this is the active ingredient in the cleaner/sanitizer that is supposed to be used at the facility. Initially PIC thought test strips were bad because they were not registering a color change when checking concentration. Inspector’s quat test strips were used to verify proper concentration of quaternary ammonia sanitizer at 200ppm. Ensure quat test strips are also available for use if there is potential for quat product to be substituted for DDBSA/lactic acid product depending on available supplies.
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Container of cheese shreds sitting on top of ice at the make line was observed with a surface temperature of 53F. Upon stirring product and taking internal temperature cheese shreds were observed at 43F-44F in the bottom of the pan and 48F-50F in the center. Shreds were put out for service prior to lunch and were discarded. Manager was advised on use of ice baths and ensuring containers are submerged in ice as opposed to sitting with only the bottom of the pan in contact with ice. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizer in the 3 part sink and sani buckets to have a concentration of 0ppm of lactic acid. The pump on the 3 part sink was not working properly. Ensure chemical sanitizer for lactic acid meets the concentrations given in the label and manufacturer’s instructions. The sanitizer will be mixed manually until the 3 part sink dispenser can be serviced. New sanitizer concentrations were made during the inspection. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed non food prep tables to have food debris accumulation under and around equipment. 2) Observed the To Go container holder on the front line to have food debris soiling it. Holders were taken to dish during inspection. Clean non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> 1) Observed plates soiled with food spillage stored on the clean dish drying rack. 2) Observed the top shelf of dishes on the dish drying rack to be stored food contact surface up. Store dishes with the food contact surface inverted or protected from potential contamination.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a box of To Go trays and a box of plastic gallon jugs stored on the floor near the bag in box soda racks. These items were moved to at least 6" above the floor during inspection. Store single service items at least 6" off the floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floors to be soiled in the following areas: 1) under the convection oven with standing water, 2) under the bag in box soda racks with standing water, 3) under the shelves in the walk in cooler with debris. 4) The floor drain in front of the ice machine is soiled. Clean the floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
